newsitem.title: USA: US Midco products stay firm with NYMEX, diffs ease.
newsitem.headline: US Midco products stay firm with NYMEX, diffs ease.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot product prices continued their sharp increase late Wednesday, lifted by a report of falling U.S. inventories and lower production from Gulf Coast refineries, traders said.

Differentials for unleaded gasoline in Chicago came off their morning highs but remained 0.75 cent above Tuesday values. Rising gasoline futures, which settled 2.57 cents a gallon higher, squeezed the basis.
Chicago unleaded was offered at about 8.00 cents above the print, while Group Three material commanded 6.00 to 6.25 cents over.

The American Petroleum Institute (API) reported falling refinery capacity nationwide, with outages continuing in the Gulf and gasoline yields seasonally lower. Gulf Coast "M4"-grade conventional stood two cents over Tuesday's print and 5.00 cents above Monday, traders said.
"Gasoline is the story because Colonial is shipping distillate on that line," to New York Harbor, reducing supplies going to the Midwest, a trader said.
Refinery capacity fell 3.2 percentage points to 90.7 percent last week, according to API data.
Meanwhile, U.S. distillate stocks fell 827,000 barrels for the week ended November 8.
Differentials for Group Three and Chicago low sulfur diesel remained 4.0 cents over December heating oil, players said, as demand from the agricultural sector fell in the Midwest.
